minutes.headline: Select Board voted unanimously to reallocate ARPA surpluses to cover two roof overruns and committed funds to equipment purchases.
minutes.summary: The board spent the meeting reviewing every outstanding ARPA allocation ahead of the 12/31 deadline: what came in under, what is returning, and where the money could go. It voted to move surplus funds to cover the Town Hall and Senior Center roof overruns, and to commit a set of emergency-list equipment purchases. The proposal to put ARPA money into DPW tree removal waits on Town Counsel's opinion, and the interest question and the larger request list were sent back for Tuesday.

public_comment.topic: Urged bringing pay and vacation time for new employees to the next town meeting for recruitment, and asked for a report on why the Personnel Board resigned en masse.

votes.motion: Reallocate ARPA surpluses to cover capital overruns (Town Hall and Senior Center roofs) as presented.

Commit ARPA funds for a list of equipment purchases (body cameras, power stretcher and loader, radios, stair chair, cement mixer, mini excavator and trailer, school pickup truck with plow, window safety film, Council on Aging generator fence).

budget_items.what_was_said: Remaining balance of the town meeting appropriation will pay outstanding OPM and design firm bills, with some left for contingency.

IV pumps, public safety furniture, Historical Society tree removal, DPW garage floor, roof and tree removal, and Council on Aging items reported with balances or contract amounts.
Surpluses from several ARPA projects would cover the Town Hall and Senior Center roof overruns.
Library envelope and teen center leftovers would go to DPW tree removal so operating money could serve as post-12/31 contingency.
About 800,000 needs reallocating; members disputed whether roughly 350,000 of interest was already allocated, and staff will rebuild the numbers.
Chair plugged items into the list to get near the available amount; COVID payments were padded above the expected amount.
Items read out with prices and totalled before the motion.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted unanimously to move surplus ARPA funds to cover overruns on the Town Hall and Senior Center roofs.
The board voted unanimously to commit ARPA funds to a list of equipment purchases, including body cameras, a power stretcher and radios.
Using ARPA money for DPW tree removal was put off until Tuesday, pending Town Counsel's opinion on whether ARPA rules allow it.
Members disagreed on whether interest earned on the ARPA funds was already allocated, so staff will rebuild the original allocation from scratch.
Staff will try to bring updated numbers, a full ARPA accounting, the interest answer and the Town Counsel opinion on Tuesday.

why_it_matters: ARPA money has a 12/31 deadline, so these reallocations decide which one-time town projects and purchases get paid for without a new appropriation or a draw on local funds.
The unresolved interest question and the tree removal opinion mean the amount still available to reallocate is not yet settled, and the board's Tuesday choices will rest on those answers.
watch_next: The Tuesday Select Board meeting: Town Counsel's opinion on ARPA tree removal and the rebuilt ARPA accounting, including the interest.
The Munis cloud deployment quote, which had not arrived, and the larger ARPA request list sent back for Tuesday.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on both non-procedural votes (reallocate surpluses to cover roof overruns, and commit $387,565 of ARPA funds for equipment) and on the main ARPA balances. The official minutes leave out most of the discussion, including the $55,200 reallocation amount, the tree-removal idea, the Munis figures and the Town Counsel review, and they print a 5-0-0 vote beside only four named members present.
